source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Limit contact with the infant because seeing or holding the baby generally intensifies bereavement and should be avoided.","B":"Use a standard contact and memorial routine for families after stillbirth so staff can provide consistent bereavement care.","C":"Delay discussion of remembrance or cultural practices until discharge so the family can first process the loss.","D":"Offer the opportunity to hold the infant and follow desired cultural or religious practices while providing individualized support."}}
source_row.rationale: ACOG/SMFM stillbirth guidance recommends individualized bereavement care and giving parents the opportunity to hold the baby and participate in desired cultural or religious activities. Option D follows that approach without making contact obligatory. Option A restricts contact rather than offering choice. Option B ignores individual, cultural, and religious needs. Option C postpones supportive options that should be discussed during the hospitalization.
source_row.source_detail: ACOG/SMFM Management of Stillbirth — bereavement care should be individualized for personal/cultural/religious needs; parents should be offered the opportunity to hold the baby and perform desired cultural/religious activities. ACOG/SMFM Obstetric Care Consensus Management of Stillbirth, reaffirmed 2025; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Psychosocial Integrity; coping, support systems, grief/loss and therapeutic adaptation activities as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
source_row.stem: After a stillbirth, which nursing approach best reflects recommended bereavement care?
